title: I have written a new wrapper tool for retry-autopkgtest-regressions, called
description:
I have written a new wrapper tool for retry-autopkgtest-regressions, called
retry-autopkgtest. It is a friendly and easy to use tool, with nice output.

During my SRU shift I used to retry autopkgtest regressions manually for all
stable releases in the web browser, clicking one recycle link at a time. This
ended up driving me mad, especially recently, with all the increased test
failures from the infrastructure switch, and also all the linux-* packages
taking up a lot of space in britney output, it took a lot of mental work to find
the next regression to retry.

Mental work I should be using to process SRUs.

So I stated using retry-autopkgtest-regressions, and after taking a while to
figure out how to get my cookie out of my firefox cookies.sqlite database, it
worked great. It literally saved so much time.

But the problem is, the output isn't very pretty, and the format moves a lot,
and its hard to see what the HTTP status codes are.

I started using this very long one liner instead:

retry-autopkgtest-regressions --series resolute | sed '/trigger=linux-/d' | vipe | xargs -rn1 -P10 curl --cookie ~/.cache/autopkgtest.cookie -o /dev/null --silent --head --write-out '%{url_effective} : %{http_code} \n' | awk '
  NR == 1 { 
    match($0, /release=([^& ]+)/, r);
    print "SERIES\t" r[1] "\nSTATUS\tTRIGGER\tPACKAGE\tARCH" 
  }
  {
    gsub(/%2F/, "/"); gsub(/%2B/, "+");
    match($0, /package=([^& ]+)/, p);
    match($0, /trigger=([^& ]+)/, t);
    match($0, /arch=([^& ]+)/, a);
    match($0, /:[[:space:]]*([0-9]+)/, s);
    
    print s[1] "\t" t[1] "\t" p[1] "\t" a[1]
  }
' | column -t -s $'\t'

Awesome right?

It does the job, but I was annoyed at copying and pasting the whole thing each
time I wanted to run it, and I remember mwhudson's lightning talk about making
all bash scripts proper python programs, and thought I should make a proper
python program out of it.

The help page shows what parameters are implemented, and has some sample output
from a recent jammy run.

Please try it out, let me know if you like it. I recommend starting with
--dry-run before you start doing any live runs.

$ ./retry-autopkgtest
retry-autopkgtest
Author: Matthew Ruffell <email address hidden>

Re-run all autopkgtest regressions using retry-autopkgtest-regressions in a 
friendly and easy to use way.

Sign into autopkgtest.ubuntu.com with firefox to get your authenticated cookie.

Then, save it locally to ~/.cache/autopkgtest.cookie by running:
 ./retry-autopkgtest --write-cookie
Note, you can also select a specific cookie db by passing it in:
 ./retry-autopkgtest --write-cookie ~/snap/firefox/common/.mozilla/firefox/12abcdef.default/cookies.sqlite

Now you are ready to retry all autopkgtests per series.
 
 ./retry-autopkgtest --series jammy
 SERIES  jammy
 STATUS  TRIGGER                                     PACKAGE                 ARCH
 200     wireless-regdb/2026.02.04-0ubuntu1~22.04.1  linux-hwe-6.5           arm64
 200     wireless-regdb/2026.02.04-0ubuntu1~22.04.1  linux-nvidia-tegra-igx  arm64
 200     gdb/12.1-0ubuntu1~22.04.3                   rustc-1.91              s390x
 200     mailman-hyperkitty/1.2.1-1~ubuntu22.04.1    mailman-hyperkitty      i386
 200     mailman3/3.3.8-1ubuntu1~22.04.1             mailman3                amd64

Alternatively, process all stable supported series consecutively:
 ./retry-autopkgtest --all-stable-series
 
You can also run against the current devel branch by running:
 ./retry-autopkgtest --series devel
 
Dry run is available by appending --dry-run to any command:
 ./retry-autopkgtest --all-stable-series --dry-run 
 
You can edit the URL list manually like the vipe workflow by adding --editor:
 ./retry-autopkgtest --all-stable-series --editor
Note, you can also select a specific editor by passing it in:
 ./retry-autopkgtest --all-stable-series --editor vim
 
Advanced users: You can specify any flag from retry-autopkgtest-regressions
and they will be passed through directly, for example:
 ./retry-autopkgtest --series jammy --blocks wireless-regdb

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# Re-run all autopkgtests using retry-autopkgtest-regressions in
+# a friendly and easy to use way.
+# Copyright (C) 2026 Canonical Ltd.
+# Author: Matthew Ruffell <matthew.ruffell@canonical.com>

+# MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.  See the
+# GNU General Public License for more details.
+#

+# along with this program.  If not, see <http://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
+
+import os
+import sys
+import re
+import argparse
+import tempfile
+import sqlite3
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import concurrent.futures
+
+# Attempt to import the native distro-info library
+try:
+    import distro_info
+except ImportError:
+    distro_info = None
+
+USAGE_TEXT = """retry-autopkgtest
+Author: Matthew Ruffell <matthew.ruffell@canonical.com>
+
+Re-run all autopkgtest regressions using retry-autopkgtest-regressions in a
+friendly and easy to use way.
+
+Sign into autopkgtest.ubuntu.com with firefox to get your authenticated cookie.
+
+Then, save it locally to ~/.cache/autopkgtest.cookie by running:
+ ./retry-autopkgtest --write-cookie
+Note, you can also select a specific cookie db by passing it in:
+ ./retry-autopkgtest --write-cookie ~/snap/firefox/common/.mozilla/firefox/12abcdef.default/cookies.sqlite
+
+Now you are ready to retry all autopkgtests per series.
+
+ ./retry-autopkgtest --series jammy
+ SERIES  jammy
+ STATUS  TRIGGER                                     PACKAGE                 ARCH
+ 200     wireless-regdb/2026.02.04-0ubuntu1~22.04.1  linux-hwe-6.5           arm64
+ 200     wireless-regdb/2026.02.04-0ubuntu1~22.04.1  linux-nvidia-tegra-igx  arm64
+ 200     gdb/12.1-0ubuntu1~22.04.3                   rustc-1.91              s390x
+ 200     mailman-hyperkitty/1.2.1-1~ubuntu22.04.1    mailman-hyperkitty      i386
+ 200     mailman3/3.3.8-1ubuntu1~22.04.1             mailman3                amd64
+
+Alternatively, process all stable supported series consecutively:
+ ./retry-autopkgtest --all-stable-series
+
+You can also run against the current devel branch by running:
+ ./retry-autopkgtest --series devel
+
+Dry run is available by appending --dry-run to any command:
+ ./retry-autopkgtest --all-stable-series --dry-run
+
+You can edit the URL list manually like the vipe workflow by adding --editor:
+ ./retry-autopkgtest --all-stable-series --editor
+Note, you can also select a specific editor by passing it in:
+ ./retry-autopkgtest --all-stable-series --editor vim
+
+Advanced users: You can specify any flag from retry-autopkgtest-regressions
+and they will be passed through directly, for example:
+ ./retry-autopkgtest --series jammy --blocks wireless-regdb
+"""
+
+def parse_arguments():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description="Fetch, edit, and format autopkgtest regressions data."
+    )
+
+    # Intercept the standard help printer to display your exact text layout
+    parser.print_help = lambda file=None: print(USAGE_TEXT)
+
+    # If no arguments are provided at all, print help and exit
+    if len(sys.argv) == 1:
+        parser.print_help()
+        sys.exit(0)
+
+    # Core wrapper options
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "-s", "--series",
+        required=False,
+        help="The release series to pass to retry-autopkgtest-regressions (e.g., resolute, devel)"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--all-stable-series",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="Run sequentially for all supported stable releases, omitting the development branch."
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--write-cookie",
+        nargs="?",
+        const="auto",
+        default=None,
+        help="Extract session cookie from Firefox cookies.sqlite. Provide an optional path, or omit it for auto-detection."
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--dry-run",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="Skip executing the actual curl requests and instead mock status codes as 200 to preview formatting."
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--editor",
+        nargs="?",
+        const="auto",
+        default=None,
+        help="Enable interactive editing of targets before execution (like vipe). Pass an optional editor name (e.g., nano) or leave blank to use your system default ($EDITOR)."
+    )
+
+    # Options forwarded straight to retry-autopkgtest-regressions
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--all-proposed",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="run tests against all of proposed, i.e. with disabling apt pinning",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--add-trigger",
+        action="append",
+        help="add trigger(s) with a $PKG/$VERSION combo",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--state",
+        default=[],
+        help="Generate commands for given test state. --state=RUNNING also enables triggering already queued and running tests",
+        nargs="+",
+        action="extend",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--max-age",
+        type=float,
+        metavar="DAYS",
+        help="only consider candidates which are at most this number of days old (float allowed)",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--min-age",
+        type=float,
+        metavar="DAYS",
+        help="only consider candidates which are at least this number of days old (float allowed)",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--blocks",
+        help="rerun only those tests that were triggered by the named package",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--blocked-by",
+        help="rerun only those tests that are blocked by (rdeps of) the named package",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--blocked-by-tests",
+        help="rerun only those tests that are blocked by test failures of the named package",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--no-proposed",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="run tests against release+updates instead of against proposed, to re-establish a baseline for the test.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--only-unknown",
+        action="store_true",
+        help='only include tests with version of "unknown".',
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--log-regex",
+        default=None,
+        help="only consider tests with logs matching the (Python) regular expression",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--run-autopkgtest",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="for administrators: Generate run-autopkgtest commands to be run on the controller host.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--force-cached",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="Do not try to download files again, use cached version when it is present.",
+    )
+
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    return args
+
+def build_forwarded_args(args):
+    """Rebuilds parsed arguments into a clean list layout to pass down via subprocess."""
+    forwarded = []
+    if args.all_proposed:
+        forwarded.append("--all-proposed")
+    if args.add_trigger:
+        for trigger in args.add_trigger:
+            forwarded.extend(["--add-trigger", trigger])
+    if args.state:
+        forwarded.append("--state")
+        forwarded.extend(args.state)
+    if args.max_age is not None:
+        forwarded.extend(["--max-age", str(args.max_age)])
+    if args.min_age is not None:
+        forwarded.extend(["--min-age", str(args.min_age)])
+    if args.blocks:
+        forwarded.extend(["--blocks", args.blocks])
+    if args.blocked_by:
+        forwarded.extend(["--blocked-by", args.blocked_by])
+    if args.blocked_by_tests:
+        forwarded.extend(["--blocked-by-tests", args.blocked_by_tests])
+    if args.no_proposed:
+        forwarded.append("--no-proposed")
+    if args.only_unknown:
+        forwarded.append("--only-unknown")
+    if args.log_regex:
+        forwarded.extend(["--log-regex", args.log_regex])
+    if args.run_autopkgtest:
+        forwarded.append("--run-autopkgtest")
+    if args.force_cached:
+        forwarded.append("--force-cached")
+    return forwarded
+
+def find_cookies_sqlite():
+    """Searches standard and snap installation paths for Firefox cookies.sqlite."""
+    search_paths = [
+        os.path.expanduser("~/.mozilla/firefox"),
+        os.path.expanduser("~/snap/firefox/common/.mozilla/firefox")
+    ]
+
+    found_files = []
+    for base_path in search_paths:
+        if os.path.exists(base_path):
+            for root, _, files in os.walk(base_path):
+                if "cookies.sqlite" in files:
+                    found_files.append(os.path.join(root, "cookies.sqlite"))
+
+    if not found_files:
+        return None
+
+    # Sort files by modification time so we pick the most active/recent profile
+    found_files.sort(key=os.path.getmtime, reverse=True)
+    return found_files[0]
+
+def extract_and_write_cookie(sqlite_path):
+    """Safely extracts the session token and writes it in Netscape cookie format."""
+    if not os.path.exists(sqlite_path):
+        print(f"Error: File not found at {sqlite_path}", file=sys.stderr)
+        sys.exit(1)
+
+    # Firefox locks cookies.sqlite when running. We copy it to a tempfile to bypass this lock.
+    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False) as tf:
+        temp_db_path = tf.name
+
+    try:
+        shutil.copyfile(sqlite_path, temp_db_path)
+        conn = sqlite3.connect(temp_db_path)
+        cursor = conn.cursor()
+
+        # Querying with a loose host condition in case Firefox uses a leading dot (.autopkgtest.ubuntu.com)
+        cursor.execute(
+            "SELECT value FROM moz_cookies WHERE host LIKE :host AND name = :name",
+            {"host": "%autopkgtest.ubuntu.com", "name": "session"}
+        )
+        row = cursor.fetchone()
+
+        # Fallback if the cookie name is stored differently under that host
+        if not row:
+            cursor.execute(
+                "SELECT value FROM moz_cookies WHERE host LIKE :host",
+                {"host": "%autopkgtest.ubuntu.com"}
+            )
+            row = cursor.fetchone()
+
+        conn.close()
+    finally:
+        if os.path.exists(temp_db_path):
+            os.unlink(temp_db_path)
+
+    if not row or not row[0]:
+        print("Error: Could not find an active autopkgtest session cookie inside the database.", file=sys.stderr)
+        print("Please make sure you have logged into autopkgtest.ubuntu.com on Firefox first.", file=sys.stderr)
+        sys.exit(1)
+
+    session_token = row[0]
+    cookie_out_path = os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/autopkgtest.cookie")
+
+    # Ensure directory exists
+    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(cookie_out_path), exist_ok=True)
+
+    # Format matches your exact Netscape specification string
+    cookie_content = f"autopkgtest.ubuntu.com\tTRUE\t/\tTRUE\t0\tsession\t{session_token}\n"
+
+    with open(cookie_out_path, "w") as f:
+        f.write(cookie_content)
+
+    print(f"Successfully generated cookie file at: {cookie_out_path}")
+
+def run_initial_command(series, extra_args):
+    """Runs the initial regressions command passing extra arguments, and grabs its output."""
+    # Find the real location of this wrapper script
+    script_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__))
+    local_binary = os.path.join(script_dir, "retry-autopkgtest-regressions")
+
+    # Dynamic lookup: Check local directory first, then fallback to systemic $PATH search
+    if os.path.exists(local_binary) and os.access(local_binary, os.X_OK):
+        executable = local_binary
+    elif shutil.which("retry-autopkgtest-regressions"):
+        executable = "retry-autopkgtest-regressions"
+    else:
+        print("Error: 'retry-autopkgtest-regressions' command could not be found.", file=sys.stderr)
+        print("It is neither co-located with this script nor available in your system $PATH.", file=sys.stderr)
+        sys.exit(1)
+
+    cmd = [executable, "--series", series] + extra_args
+    try:
+        result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
+        return result.stdout.splitlines()
+    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
+        print(f"Error running command: {e.stderr}", file=sys.stderr)
+        sys.exit(e.returncode)
+
+def run_vipe_emulation(lines, editor_choice):
+    """Spawns an interactive editor allowing you to drop/modify lines mid-flight."""
+    if editor_choice == "auto":
+        editor = os.environ.get("VISUAL", os.environ.get("EDITOR", "vi"))
+    else:
+        editor = editor_choice
+
+    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w+", suffix=".txt", delete=False) as temp_file:
+        temp_file.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
+        temp_path = temp_file.name
+
+    try:
+        # Opens the editor interactively attached directly to your terminal TTY
+        subprocess.run([editor, temp_path], check=True)
+        with open(temp_path, "r") as temp_file:
+            updated_lines = temp_file.read().splitlines()
+    except FileNotFoundError:
+        print(f"Error: Specified editor '{editor}' was not found on your system.", file=sys.stderr)
+        return lines
+    finally:
+        if os.path.exists(temp_path):
+            os.unlink(temp_path)
+
+    # Drop empty lines
+    return [line for line in updated_lines if line.strip()]
+
+def fetch_url_status(url):
+    """Performs the concurrent curl request mapping perfectly to your xargs setup."""
+    cookie_path = os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/autopkgtest.cookie")
+    cmd = [
+        "curl",
+        "--cookie", cookie_path,
+        "-o", "/dev/null",
+        "--silent",
+        "--head",
+        "--write-out", "%{url_effective} status=%{http_code}",
+        url
+    ]
+    res = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
+    return res.stdout.strip()
+
+def parse_and_decode(raw_line):
+    """Decodes standard symbols and uses regex to isolate targets (like awk did)."""
+    # Replace URL encoded structures (%2F -> /, %2B -> + and %3A -> :)
+    decoded = raw_line.replace("%2F", "/").replace("%2B", "+").replace("%3A", ":")
+
+    pkg = re.search(r"package=([^& ]+)", decoded)
+    trig = re.search(r"trigger=([^& ]+)", decoded)
+    arch = re.search(r"arch=([^& ]+)", decoded)
+    stat = re.search(r"status=([0-9]+)", decoded)
+    rel = re.search(r"release=([^& ]+)", decoded)
+
+    return {
+        "package": pkg.group(1) if pkg else "",
+        "trigger": trig.group(1) if trig else "",
+        "arch": arch.group(1) if arch else "",
+        "status": stat.group(1) if stat else "",
+        "release": rel.group(1) if rel else ""
+    }
+
+def print_formatted_table(parsed_rows, fallback_series=""):
+    """Emulates column -t layout constraints dynamically."""
+    if not parsed_rows:
+        return
+
+    release_name = parsed_rows[0]["release"] if parsed_rows[0]["release"] else fallback_series
+
+    # Construct the data layout grid
+    matrix = []
+    matrix.append(["SERIES", release_name])
+    matrix.append(["STATUS", "TRIGGER", "PACKAGE", "ARCH"])
+
+    for row in parsed_rows:
+        matrix.append([row["status"], row["trigger"], row["package"], row["arch"]])
+
+    # Calculate target column widths dynamically based on maximum lengths
+    col_widths = [0] * 4
+    for row in matrix:
+        for i, cell in enumerate(row):
+            if len(cell) > col_widths[i]:
+                col_widths[i] = len(cell)
+
+    # Output formatted string data with standard 2-space padding boundaries
+    for row in matrix:
+        line_parts = []
+        for i, cell in enumerate(row):
+            if i < len(row) - 1:
+                line_parts.append(cell.ljust(col_widths[i] + 2))
+            else:
+                line_parts.append(cell)
+        print("".join(line_parts).rstrip())
+
+def process_series(series, dry_run=False, editor_choice=None, extra_args=None):
+    """Executes the standard pipeline workflow for an explicit Ubuntu series."""
+    if extra_args is None:
+        extra_args = []
+
+    # 1. Fetch initial output lines (passing extra args to underlying script)
+    raw_lines = run_initial_command(series, extra_args)
+
+    # 2. Filter data matching your sed '/trigger=linux-/d' constraint
+    filtered_lines = [line for line in raw_lines if "trigger=linux-" not in line]
+
+    if not filtered_lines:
+        print(f"SERIES\t{series}")
+        print("No matches remaining after 'trigger=linux-' filtering.\n")
+        return
+
+    # 3. Handle Interactive Editor Logic
+    if editor_choice is not None:
+        editable_urls = run_vipe_emulation(filtered_lines, editor_choice)
+        if not editable_urls:
+            print(f"SERIES\t{series}")
+            print("Pipeline aborted or all records deleted inside the editor.\n")
+            return
+    else:
+        editable_urls = filtered_lines
+
+    # 4. Generate outputs (Mocked via dry-run or processed concurrently via curl)
+    curl_outputs = []
+    if dry_run:
+        print(f"[Dry Run] Mocking URL statuses as 200 for {series}...", file=sys.stderr)
+        curl_outputs = [f"{url} status=200" for url in editable_urls]
+    else:
+        # ThreadPoolExecutor.map preserves the absolute input list order naturally
+        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=10) as executor:
+            results = executor.map(fetch_url_status, editable_urls)
+            for res in results:
+                if res:
+                    curl_outputs.append(res)
+
+    # 5. Extract structures and output structured table results in their original chronological order
+    parsed_rows = [parse_and_decode(line) for line in curl_outputs]
+
+    print_formatted_table(parsed_rows, fallback_series=series)
+    print()  # Breathing room between stacked outputs
+
+def main():
+    args = parse_arguments()
+
+    # Check if we are running the cookie initialization branch
+    if args.write_cookie is not None:
+        if args.write_cookie == "auto":
+            print("Auto-detecting Firefox profile database...")
+            db_path = find_cookies_sqlite()
+            if not db_path:
+                print("Error: Could not automatically locate your Firefox cookies.sqlite file.", file=sys.stderr)
+                print("Please supply the path manually, for example:", file=sys.stderr)
+                print("  ./retry-autopkgtest.py --write-cookie ~/snap/firefox/common/.mozilla/firefox/xyz.default/cookies.sqlite", file=sys.stderr)
+                sys.exit(1)
+            print(f"Auto-detected database target: {db_path}")
+        else:
+            db_path = os.path.expanduser(args.write_cookie)
+
+        extract_and_write_cookie(db_path)
+        return
+
+    # Validate that the authenticated cookie file exists unless doing a dry run
+    if not args.dry_run:
+        cookie_path = os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/autopkgtest.cookie")
+        if not os.path.exists(cookie_path):
+            print("Error: Authenticated cookie file not found at ~/.cache/autopkgtest.cookie", file=sys.stderr)
+            print("Please sign into autopkgtest.ubuntu.com with Firefox first, then run:", file=sys.stderr)
+            print("  ./retry-autopkgtest --write-cookie", file=sys.stderr)
+            sys.exit(1)
+
+    # Normal routine safety validations
+    if not args.series and not args.all_stable_series:
+        print("Error: one of the following arguments is required: -s/--series or --all-stable-series (unless using --write-cookie)", file=sys.stderr)
+        sys.exit(1)
+
+    if args.series and args.all_stable_series:
+        print("Error: Arguments --series and --all-stable-series are mutually exclusive.", file=sys.stderr)
+        sys.exit(1)
+
+    # Compile the clean list of parameters targeted for retry-autopkgtest-regressions
+    extra_args = build_forwarded_args(args)
+
+    # Determine series distribution list targets
+    target_series = []
+
+    if args.all_stable_series:
+        if not distro_info:
